title: Field Service Policy for Hospital Beds & Support Surfaces: Maintenance, Repairs and Warranty
content:
Preventive maintenance with the entrapment check is performed on every Hospital Beds & Support Surfaces bed in the home at the class's maintenance interval in months. While a bed is rented (coverage or private), every repair is Summit Ridge's obligation at no charge, completed or swapped within the class's rental repair-or-swap business days. On an owned bed, the class's frame warranty and electrical (motor and hand pendant) warranty apply first, both counted from the delivery date; out of warranty, labor at the class's labor rate per unit plus parts is billed to the coverage, with the patient owing the cost share, and a repair costing more than the class's repair cost limit percentage of the class's fee-schedule purchase amount is not made. A service visit is recorded only on a bed in the home: the bed record is rental active, suspended or patient owned.

The interval, warranty months, labor rate, repair cost limit and repair-or-swap days are the bed class's published service figures; the purchase amount is the class's fee-schedule purchase amount.

## Who bears a repair

| Bed's standing | Repair |
|---|---|
| Rented on coverage | Summit Ridge's obligation at no charge; completed or swapped within the class's business days |
| Rented privately | Summit Ridge's obligation at no charge; completed or swapped within the class's business days |
| Owned, within the frame or electrical warranty for the part concerned | The warranty applies first |
| Owned, out of warranty | Labor per unit plus parts billed to the coverage; the patient owes the cost share |
| Owned, repair costing more than the limit percentage of the purchase amount | Not made |

## Recording a service visit

| Status of the bed record | Service visit recorded |
|---|---|
| rental active | Yes |
| suspended | Yes |
| patient owned | Yes |
| order received, returned or cancelled | No |

The status is read from the bed record in the system before the visit is recorded.

## Worked example (hypothetical repair)

Hypothetical inputs: an owned Semi-Electric Hospital Bed (E0260) outside both warranties; 6 labor units at the published rate of $23.86 per unit; parts of $210.00; a fee-schedule purchase amount of $1486.40 and a repair cost limit of 100 percent.

- Labor: 6 units multiplied by $23.86 is $143.16.
- Labor plus parts: $143.16 and $210.00 total $353.16.
- The limit: 100 percent of $1486.40 is $1486.40. The repair cost of $353.16 is not more than the limit, so the not-made rule does not reach it; the labor and parts are billed to the coverage and the patient owes the cost share.
- A hypothetical repair estimated at $1600.00 on the same bed costs more than $1486.40 and is not made.

## Warranty periods (hypothetical delivery)

For an owned bed delivered on a hypothetical 5 June, both warranties are counted from that delivery date: a 12-month electrical warranty runs 12 calendar months from 5 June, and a 60-month frame warranty runs 60 calendar months from 5 June.
